key_insight: Gradient flow can predict recovery after pretraining, but finite-batch SGD can still fail because rare ReLU gate disagreements dominate the target-task dynamics.
engineering_relevance: For transfer learning and plasticity analysis, batch size, step size, and pretraining duration jointly control whether a model can actually adapt after source-task training.
method: Two-unit ReLU regression with a source task that aligns neurons and a target task that separates them
Compare population gradient flow vs online SGD with finite batch and step size across pretraining and adaptation
Track the rare wedge of inputs where ReLU gates disagree and bound its cumulative sampling probability exactly
evidence_signal: The abstract reports high-probability recovery failure over horizons of order e^{c/η} once T ≳ log(b/η), and simulations show recovery is mainly governed by the disagreement budget bδ/η.
watch_item: The result is proved in a simplified two-unit ReLU setting, so translating the failure mode to larger architectures may require care.
paper_title: Rare Gate Disagreements Can Limit Plasticity: When Gradient Flow Mispredicts Finite-Batch SGD
